title: PUT can mutate soft-deleted feeds into inconsistent active tombstones

evidence.quote: Returns all feeds regardless of active status (excludes tombstoned feeds).

feed.is_active = False
    feed.deleted_at = now
    feed.updated_at = now

reasoning: The route updates any row returned by primary key, including rows that have been soft-deleted. Deletion marks a feed inactive and sets deleted_at, while list/changes treat deleted_at as the tombstone state and create_feed explicitly clears deleted_at when restoring. PUT does not reject tombstoned rows or clear deleted_at, so a client can send {"is_active": true} after deletion and leave the row simultaneously active and tombstoned. That makes subsequent sync/list behavior inconsistent and can hide an apparently active feed from normal feed listings.
reproduction: Create a feed, DELETE /api/feeds/{id}, then PUT /api/feeds/{id} with {"is_active": true}. The response will be 200 with is_active true while deleted_at remains set; GET /api/feeds still excludes it because deleted_at is not null.
recommendation: In update_feed, either return 404/410 for feeds with deleted_at set, or implement an explicit restore path that clears deleted_at atomically when reactivating. Keep the behavior aligned with create_feed's restore semantics.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_feeds.py only covers listing, creation, and sync. It has no PUT or delete-then-update coverage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates a feed, deletes it, then verifies PUT /api/feeds/{id} cannot leave is_active=true with deleted_at still set; assert either 404/410 or restored deleted_at=null behavior, depending on the intended contract.
minimumFixScope: app/api/feeds.py update_feed plus focused tests in tests/test_feeds.py
